questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study in USA and especially California. I wanted to study a place with warmer weather.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: In general, it was easy. There was some difficulties with signing up for courses and waitlists on courses, but it worked out and the university helped us.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance regarding visa rules, safety, the university facilities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They could have given us more social orientation. We only had one day, which was very packed with a lot of information. They could have given us more time to just get to know the other exchange students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult. I did not find until I arrived, and I stayed at a hotel the first week. I found through Airbnb. Housing is very expensive. There is a big risk of being scammed, so it is difficult to find housing before you are actually in the city.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Depending on what neighborhood you choose to live in, it is a lot more safer and nicer than the neighborhood campus is in. Campus was also quite expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They told us from the beginning that it was not possible for exchange students to live on campus because it was reserved for long time students. But when we arrived they suddenly had housing and said there we could stay there, but then we had already found our own.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Exchange students were the very last to sign up for courses after the LLM students and JD students. This meant that almost all courses had waitlists when we could sign up which was stressful. I had to apply for pre approval for more courses just to be sure. Students could sign up for way more credits than needed, so I had the impression that maybe people had a lot of back up plans, which just made a lot of waitlists. But it ended up being fine.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university was very helpful both when we arrived and when I had questions regarding the courses for my pre approval. We had a one on one meeting where we looked at our schedule. It was also possible for the university to make an extra spot for en exchange if the class was full.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: See above regarding the waitlists. But I ended up getting 3 out of 4 of the courses I had looked at, and the last I had to find after I arrived and get a new pre approval for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: We talked with the university about the waitlist situation, so maybe they will change it. But otherwise let the future exchange student know about the waitlist, so it is not as stressful for them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It took two classes with first year students, and two classes with second and third years. The level was easy in all classes. Especially with the first years, they took it from scratch because it was the students' first year of law school.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: First, attendance is required in all courses. Second, participation is required in most classes. They use cold calling, where the professor just pick a random from the class to answer or explain a case.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Contracts, torts, international human rights, and real estate transactions.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It would recommend all of them. Contracts and torts are basic and general American law, and it gives a good perspective on the American law. I enjoyed comparing it to what I have learned from my danish courses. International human rights is relevant because it mostly is also applicable for Denmark, and it is relatable. Regarding real estate transaction, it was good to learn the concepts of real estate and the measurements (more economic also), but a big part of it was regarding what company should be chosen for different structures and tax law, which is not that important and relevant for an exchange student to know. But the professor in the class was very nice.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Be aware that there is fees on everything. There is a very high tipping culture of 15-20 %. 
I had my Danish insurance approved. But if they had not approved it, I would have had to pay 16.000 DKK for the American insurance.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Eating out was way more expensive than I expected. Even before the taxes and tips, it was more expensive that in Denmark. 
I did not find grocery shopping as expensive as I expected. 
I knew that housing was very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Because the university is in the city (I guess) there was no sports clubs, and not sports facilities as you would find on other campus.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was mostly associations either regarding a specific legal area or regarding your ethnicity.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Every second Thursday, there was beers and pizza in the quad. I would recommend going to that.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: San Francisco has a lot of different neighborhoods to explore. There is a lot to do just in the city. It is a city with shopping, cafes, restaurants, but it also has beautiful nature and the sea. Some weekends we also visited other parts of California. I have been to Lake Tahoe, Yosemite, Las Vegas, Los Angeles, Santa Barbara and other coastal cities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: In general, it was fine.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult to socialize with local students. I socialized the most with the local students in the class where I was the only exchange student. I think it would have been easier if I had lived on campus.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very friendly and out going.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It is very expensive, especially housing.

We were only 7 exchange students, which in the beginning was a bit disappointing, but we found out there was around 30 LLM students from other countries, who were in our age also. 

San Francisco has a reputation for being a bit dangerous city. The university is in the worst area with a lot homeless people and drugs. This is relevant when considering living on campus. I lived off campus in a very nice neighborhood, and I had no problems with the area the university was in, but I would not walk in the area after dark.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: When looking for housing off campus, use airbnb (and maybe get a deal outside airbnb), Craigslist and use the facebook groups.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of the exchange is meeting a lot of new friends from different parts of especially Europe. Since we were not that many exchange students, we really got to know each other and spent a lot of time together.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing off campus.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It was a very great semester abroad, and I really recommend going! San Francisco is a very nice city to stay in, and there is a lot of other things to experience in other parts on California. The weather is very nice especially in the fall.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
